# Belgium screen: where outside Brussels is there recent 360° imagery?

**Ran:** 2026-10-08 ·
**Record:** [`belgium-screen_metrics.json`](belgium-screen_metrics.json) and [`belgium-screen_places.csv`](belgium-screen_places.csv) ·
**Generated by:** `python scripts/belgium_screen_analyze.py --docs-dir docs/experiments` ·
**Collected by:** `scripts/belgium_screen_collect.py` as an offline replay of the research pass (see Provenance) ·
**Manifest:** [`belgium_inquiry_cities.csv`](../../belgium_inquiry_cities.csv).
Instruments: the [#383](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/383) Mapillary z6 sequence screen ([`mapillary-discovery-screen.md`](mapillary-discovery-screen.md)) and the [#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316) Panoramax z6 grid screen ([`panoramax-feasibility.md`](panoramax-feasibility.md), [`panoramax-world-screen.md`](panoramax-world-screen.md)).

## Verdict

**Outside Brussels-Capital, the only dense recent Mapillary 360° capture in Belgium is the Antwerp agglomeration, and it is almost all one creator.**
Antwerp scores 22.14 recent-360° km per km², with 96% of that length from its largest creator; 14 places within 15.4 km of Antwerp's point clear 7 km/km², and the top creator holds 62–100% in each.
Beyond Antwerp, only four places clear 7: Rixensart (22.63, one creator) and its neighbour Basse Lasne (7.70) in Walloon Brabant, and Gent (8.34) with its district Sint-Amandsberg (8.34).
**Panoramax 360° imagery is spread differently**: after Brussels-Capital, the largest bounds sit around Braine-l'Alleud and Waterloo, Mechelen, Boom and Rumst, and Leuven — places where Mapillary is thin.

The decision this supported: register and enable **Antwerp, Mechelen and Beringen** on production (2026-10-08, first night 2026-10-09) for a deployment inquiry about Beringen.
Beringen is the town the inquiry is about, so it was registered whatever it scored.
Antwerp is the one Flemish city with Mapillary density near the Brussels communes'; Mechelen holds the largest Panoramax 360° bound of any place in Flanders.
The road walks are what will answer the inquiry; the screen only chose which cities to walk.

## The question

Before this screen, the catalog tracked one Belgian city: Brussels, registered as the whole Brussels-Capital Region (`mapillary_360_cities.csv`).
A deployment inquiry about Beringen, a Flemish town of ~41,000, asked whether street-level imagery there is good enough for a Project Sidewalk deployment.
The question the screen answers is narrower and comes first: **which Belgian places have enough recent 360° imagery to be worth registering and walking, and where does Beringen sit among them?**

For context, Brussels' first road walks (drive network), **quoted from the production catalog, not re-derived from this record**:

| Provider | 360° street-km | any imagery street-km |
|---|---|---|
| GSV | 97.4% | — |
| Mapillary | 85.2% | 96.1% |
| Panoramax | 31.3% | 36.7% |
| KartaView | 0% | 25.4% |

## Method

### The instruments

**Mapillary.** The coverage vector tiles' `sequence` layer at z6, the #383 instrument: one simplified LineString per capture sequence, carrying `captured_at`, `creator_id` and `is_pano`.
All of Belgium (2.5..6.45°E × 49.45..51.55°N) is **two z6 tiles**, (32, 21) and (33, 21).
A sequence counts if `is_pano` is true and it was captured on or after **2024-10-08** (two years before the screen).
Each simplified segment becomes one sample at its midpoint, weighted by its full length; a place's signal is the sampled length within **2 km** of its GeoNames point, per km² of that disc (12.57 km²), plus the share of that length from its largest creator.
That is coarser than #383's analysis, which cut segments into 0.5 km pieces; it is what this pass measured, and the replay keeps it.

**Panoramax.** The v2 `grid` layer at z6 — H3 cells of measured resolution 7 (~5.2 km²) carrying `nb_pictures` and `nb_360_pictures` — over the same **two** tiles, decoded by `panoramax_screen.hexes_from_tile` and merged by `merge_hexes`.
A place's signal is the sum over every cell whose centre lies within **3 km** of its point (approximately the cells touching its 2 km disc).
**These are UPPER BOUNDS, never coverage**: a cell is counted whole, and neighbouring places share cells, so place bounds never add up to anything.

**Places.** Every GeoNames `cities500` place in Belgium with population ≥ 10,000: **n = 373** (18 in Brussels-Capital, 355 outside).
Brussels-Capital is the 18 places GeoNames files under admin-1 `BRU`, pinned by name in `belgium_screen_analyze.BRUSSELS_CAPITAL`; Woluwe-Saint-Pierre, the region's 19th commune, is not a `cities500` place and was not scored.

### Traffic

Four requests in total, from the Mac on 2026-10-08 (~14:47 UTC): the two Mapillary tiles 18 s apart (20.5 MB and 20.9 MB, both HTTP 200, through the #383 research fetcher's cache and pacer), and the two Panoramax tiles with a 2 s sleep before each (2.1 MB and 2.3 MB).
No refusal.
Nothing in this writeup required a further request, and none was made.

## Findings

### 1. Mapillary density: Brussels-Capital, then Antwerp, then almost nothing

Recent-360° km per km² over the 2 km disc (`mapillary.km_per_km2_*`):

| Population | n | min | p25 | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| All places | 373 | 0.00 | 0.23 | 0.88 | 1.98 | 6.49 | 14.79 | 51.97 |
| Brussels-Capital | 18 | 8.36 | 14.67 | 19.05 | 27.63 | 45.85 | 48.02 | 51.97 |
| Outside Brussels-Capital | 355 | 0.00 | 0.20 | 0.79 | 1.77 | 3.04 | 7.01 | 27.75 |

65 of the 373 places hold no recent 360° Mapillary sequence within 2 km at all.

**Brussels-Capital ranges from 8.36 (Berchem-Sainte-Agathe) to 51.97 (Brussels)**, not uniformly high: 14 of its 18 places clear 14, and Uccle (13.71), Watermael-Boitsfort (10.42), Auderghem (8.98) and Berchem-Sainte-Agathe (8.36) do not.
It is also the most mixed capture in the record: the largest creator holds 37–82% per place there (`mapillary.brussels_capital`), against 62–100% in every dense place outside it.

**Outside Brussels-Capital, 18 places clear 7 km/km²** (`mapillary.outside_brussels_capital_at_or_above_floor`):

| Place | km/km² | top-creator share | km from Antwerp's point |
|---|---|---|---|
| Berchem | 27.75 | 0.94 | 4.0 |
| Borgerhout | 27.49 | 0.96 | 2.7 |
| Rixensart | 22.63 | 1.00 | 56.9 |
| Antwerp | 22.14 | 0.96 | 0.0 |
| Deurne | 17.10 | 0.97 | 4.6 |
| Mortsel | 15.78 | 0.95 | 6.9 |
| Wilrijk | 14.87 | 0.96 | 5.9 |
| Edegem | 14.14 | 0.94 | 7.7 |
| Kontich | 11.74 | 0.92 | 10.3 |
| Merksem | 10.47 | 0.92 | 4.4 |
| Borsbeek | 9.43 | 1.00 | 6.5 |
| Boechout | 9.17 | 1.00 | 9.3 |
| Hoboken | 8.82 | 0.87 | 6.1 |
| Boom | 8.71 | 0.62 | 14.3 |
| Gent | 8.34 | 0.98 | 51.3 |
| Sint-Amandsberg | 8.34 | 0.93 | 48.8 |
| Rumst | 8.25 | 0.76 | 15.4 |
| Basse Lasne | 7.70 | 0.97 | 58.5 |

Fourteen of the 18 are Antwerp and its districts and suburbs.
The record holds each place's top-creator SHARE, not the creator's id, so whether one creator is behind all fourteen is **not** something it can say, only that one creator dominates each.
Every other place outside Brussels-Capital and those four is below 7.

Over the 308 places with any recent 360° length, the top-creator share is p25 0.72 and p50 **1.00** (`mapillary.top_creator_share_where_any`): in most of Belgium the recent 360° imagery near a town is one person's or one programme's drive.

### 2. Panoramax: a different map

360° upper bound per place (`panoramax.pnx_360_ub_all`): n = 373, min 0, p25 84, p50 1,318, p75 3,355, p90 7,647, p95 14,249, max 45,129 (Brussels); 82 places have a bound of zero.
Brussels-Capital places fill most of the top of the list, as with Mapillary, but outside it the ranking is unrelated to Mapillary's (`panoramax.named`):

| Place | 360° bound | all pictures bound | flat share of the bound | Mapillary km/km² |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Braine-l'Alleud | 32,360 | 35,746 | 0.095 | 0.00 |
| Waterloo | 23,681 | 24,080 | 0.017 | 0.80 |
| Mechelen | 21,605 | 21,837 | 0.011 | 2.18 |
| Rumst | 17,887 | 17,914 | 0.002 | 8.25 |
| Boom | 17,813 | 17,865 | 0.003 | 8.71 |
| Leuven | 15,973 | 17,045 | 0.063 | 1.89 |
| Menen | 14,255 | 122,812 | 0.884 | 0.33 |
| Wervik | 13,309 | 94,041 | 0.858 | 0.20 |

Boom and Rumst, 3.7 km apart (`named_pairs_km`), share most of their cells; their two bounds are one body of imagery counted twice.
Menen, Wervik and neighbouring Mouscron, on the French border, hold the three largest all-picture bounds in the record (94,041–122,812, more than any Brussels commune), but **86–92% of those pictures are flat**, not 360° (`panoramax.top_by_pictures_ub`).
Antwerp's own 360° bound is 4,832, below the national p95.

### 3. The three registered cities

| City | Mapillary km/km² | top-creator share | Panoramax 360° bound | Panoramax pictures bound |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Antwerp | 22.14 | 0.96 | 4,832 | 6,651 |
| Mechelen | 2.18 | 0.68 | 21,605 | 21,837 |
| Beringen | 1.45 | 1.00 | 4,441 | 4,485 |

(`registered`.) Beringen's Mapillary signal is 18.2 km of recent 360° sequence within 2 km, all from one creator — between the national p50 (0.88) and p75 (1.98), and about a fifteenth of Antwerp's.
Antwerp–Mechelen is 22.2 km (`registered_pairwise_km`) and Mechelen–Brussels 21.4 km (`named_pairs_km`), both inside `register_frame.py`'s default 25 km reuse radius, so the batch needed an overlap radius below 21.4 km — purposive batches use `--overlap-km 5` — or Mechelen would have been aliased onto a neighbour instead of registered; the test pins every row more than 5 km from every other committed manifest row.
Each frozen grid contains the whole 2 km disc around its GeoNames point, so the screen numbers above describe imagery inside the grid; `tests/test_belgium_inquiry_cities_manifest.py` pins that against the frozen geometry.

## What this justifies

- Registering Antwerp, Mechelen and Beringen (done 2026-10-08, notes label `belgium inquiry 2026-10-08`); all three passed the boundary audit with no resize.
- Expecting Antwerp's Mapillary walk to look like a single creator's sweep, not a city programme: high coverage for as long as that creator keeps capturing, and no redundancy if they stop.
- Not expecting Beringen to look like Brussels: its walks are the measurement, and the screen predicts a thin, single-creator Mapillary record there.

## Caveats

- **A screen, not coverage.** z6 Mapillary geometry is simplified, so lengths are approximate, and a sequence's length says nothing about which streets it covered. The Panoramax figures are upper bounds over whole cells. Only a road walk measures street coverage.
- **A 2 km disc around a GeoNames point is not a city.** It is about 12.6 km² against frozen grids of 122 km² (Mechelen, 12,553 × 9,744 m) to 530 km² (Antwerp, 20,346 × 26,072 m) — the production geometry pinned as `FROZEN_GEOMETRY` in `tests/test_belgium_inquiry_cities_manifest.py`, not part of this record.
- **"Recent" is a fixed cutoff** (captured on or after 2024-10-08); an older city-wide capture scores zero.
- **The cutoff and the density floor of 7 are choices**, not derived thresholds; the floor only decides which places this writeup lists by name.
- The Brussels walk figures in "The question" are quoted from the production catalog and are not in this record.

## Provenance

The 2026-10-08 pass was a research script kept beside its raw output, `experiments/belgium-screen-2026-10-08/screen.py` (gitignored with it).
It imported a gitignored helper from the #383 screen's raw directory for the Mapillary fetch and decode; main already holds the committed equivalents, `scripts/mapillary_discovery_common.decode_sequences` and `local_km` (and `mapillary_discovery_collect.TileFetcher` for the fetch), which is what `scripts/belgium_screen_collect.py` uses.
That script makes **no network request**: it replays the four cached tiles (the two Mapillary tiles in the #383 tile cache, the two Panoramax tiles beside the research script) and the `cities500.txt` downloaded for #383 on 2026-10-02.
**On 2026-10-08 its output was byte-identical to the research script's `belgium_places.csv`**, which is committed unchanged as `belgium-screen_places.csv`.
None of those inputs is committed (two of the tiles are ~20 MB each, and `cities500` is not vendored), so the replay can be re-run only on a machine holding that cache; everything downstream of the per-place CSV re-runs anywhere, and `tests/test_belgium_screen.py` requires the committed JSON to equal what the analysis derives from it.

## Replicating

```bash
# Re-derive the metrics from the committed per-place record (offline, anywhere):
python scripts/belgium_screen_analyze.py --docs-dir docs/experiments

# Re-derive the per-place record from the cached tiles (offline; needs the gitignored cache):
python scripts/belgium_screen_collect.py \
    --mapillary-tiles experiments/mapillary-discovery-383/tiles \
    --panoramax-tiles experiments/belgium-screen-2026-10-08 \
    --places experiments/mapillary-discovery-383/cities500.txt \
    --out docs/experiments/belgium-screen_places.csv
```

A fresh screen needs the four tiles fetched again: the Mapillary pair through `mapillary_discovery_collect.TileFetcher` (paced at a mean 40/min with CV 0.6, stopping on the first refusal), the Panoramax pair from `panoramax_screen.SCREEN_URL_TEMPLATE`.
Read [`docs/provider-access.md`](../provider-access.md) first.
